notes: As-built U-values only. Engineer should enter directly for EWI/IWI on solid walls (certified value expected).
Bands A-E solid brick: use formula_type='brick_thickness', call solidBrickUValue(thicknessMm)
Bands A-E stone: use formula_type='stone_granite' or 'stone_sandstone', call stoneUValue(thicknessMm)
Filled cavity rows are included as 'current state' regardless of when CWI was installed.
Ground floors are excluded — calculated via BS EN ISO 13370 from area/perimeter in the app.
Thermal bridging y-factors (Table 21) are stored separately, not in this library.
Age band M (2023+) values taken from M column where shown. Not all regions publish M separately.
† means assumed as-built in RdSAP source. * means applies only if insulation added subsequently.
We include † rows (they are current-state values). We exclude * rows (retrofit insulation — enter directly).
insulation_mm: only relevant for rows where added insulation changes the base as-built value.
For formula rows, u_value is null — compute at runtime using formula_type + thicknessMm.

party_walls.description: Solid masonry / timber frame / system build
party_walls.description_detail: Between identical heated dwellings. ΔT=0 in normal use; heat loss is zero. Use a custom ΔT on the element if the adjacent dwelling is unheated.
Unfilled cavity party wall. Higher U-value reflects potential air movement within the cavity.
Default where party wall construction cannot be determined.
RdSAP assumes construction avoids thermal bypass in flats/maisonettes.

floors_party.description_detail: ΔT=0 between dwellings at the same temperature. No heat loss. For floors above unheated spaces use Exposed/semi-exposed floor instead.
floors_party.notes: RdSAP10 Section 5.13: internal floors between heated dwellings are disregarded.

floors_party.description_detail: Construction U-value: 150mm dense concrete + 13mm plaster both sides. Apply a custom ΔT for the actual temperature difference to the adjacent unheated space.
floors_party.notes: First-principles per BS EN ISO 6946:2017. λ_concrete=1.35, λ_plaster=0.57 W/m·K (BS EN ISO 10456:2007).

doors_internal.description: Internal door — solid or hollow core, 35mm (standard domestic)
doors_internal.description_detail: Both solid timber and hollow core give ≈2.0 W/m²K at standard domestic thickness. Rsi=Rse=0.13 m²K/W.
doors_internal.notes: First-principles per BS EN ISO 6946:2017. Matches MCS heat load calculator internal door value.

walls_internal.description: Internal partition — timber stud with plasterboard both sides
walls_internal.description_detail: 12.5mm plasterboard, unventilated air gap, 12.5mm plasterboard. Horizontal heat flow, Rsi=Rse=0.13 m²K/W. Consistent with CIBSE DHDG 2026 Table 2-36.
walls_internal.notes: Most common UK domestic partition. For wall to adjacent heated space use customDeltaT = Ti − 15°C. For wall to unheated space use customDeltaT = Ti − 5°C.

walls_internal.description: Internal wall — 102mm brick, plaster both sides
walls_internal.description_detail: 13mm plaster, 102mm brick, 13mm plaster. Horizontal heat flow, Rsi=Rse=0.13 m²K/W. Consistent with CIBSE DHDG 2026 Table 2-36 (2.05 W/m²K).
walls_internal.notes: Single brick partition wall. Typical in older UK domestic construction.

walls_internal.description: Internal wall — 215mm brick, plaster both sides
walls_internal.description_detail: 13mm plaster, 215mm brick, 13mm plaster. Horizontal heat flow, Rsi=Rse=0.13 m²K/W. Consistent with CIBSE DHDG 2026 Table 2-36 (1.45 W/m²K).
walls_internal.notes: Double brick internal wall. May be a structural or party wall.

walls_internal.description: Internal wall — 100mm dense concrete block, plaster both sides
walls_internal.description_detail: 13mm plaster, 100mm dense concrete block, 13mm plaster. Horizontal heat flow, Rsi=Rse=0.13 m²K/W. Consistent with CIBSE DHDG 2026 Table 2-36 (2.76 W/m²K).

walls_internal.description: Internal wall — 100mm lightweight/HP aerated block, plaster both sides
walls_internal.description_detail: 13mm plaster, 100mm high-performance aerated block, 13mm plaster. Horizontal heat flow, Rsi=Rse=0.13 m²K/W. Consistent with CIBSE DHDG 2026 Table 2-36 (0.82 W/m²K).
walls_internal.notes: HP (high performance) aerated block. Common in post-1990 construction.

floors_intermediate.description: Intermediate timber floor — heat flow upwards (room below heating room above)
floors_intermediate.description_detail: 19mm boarding, airspace between joists, 9.5mm plasterboard. Upward heat flow: Rsi=Rse=0.10 m²K/W per ISO 6946. Consistent with CIBSE DHDG 2026 Table 2-45 (1.73 W/m²K).
floors_intermediate.notes: Use when the room being calculated is BELOW the intermediate floor (heat rising into cooler space above). For heat loss: ΔT = Ti(lower room) − Ti(upper room).

floors_intermediate.description: Intermediate timber floor — heat flow downwards (room above losing heat to room below)
floors_intermediate.description_detail: 19mm boarding, airspace between joists, 9.5mm plasterboard. Downward heat flow: Rsi=Rse=0.17 m²K/W per ISO 6946. Consistent with CIBSE DHDG 2026 Table 2-45 (1.41 W/m²K).
floors_intermediate.notes: Use when the room being calculated is ABOVE the intermediate floor (heat falling into cooler space below). For heat loss: ΔT = Ti(upper room) − Ti(lower room).

floors_intermediate.description: Exposed timber floor underside — heat flow downwards (to outside or unheated space)
floors_intermediate.description_detail: 19mm boarding, airspace between joists, insulation, 6mm sheeting. No insulation variant: 1.75 W/m²K. Consistent with CIBSE DHDG 2026 Table 2-45.
floors_intermediate.notes: For floors over external air or unheated void. Use RdSAP Table 20 (floor_exposed) values for age-band defaults.
